extracted.intended_audience: prospective Hertz Fellowship applicants (college seniors, first-year graduate students, or gap-period applicants intending to pursue a PhD)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and formal eligibility/selection criteria for applicants seeking the Hertz Fellowship to pursue a full-time, in-person PhD in applied physical/biological sciences, mathematics, or engineering at a U.S. institution. Covers who may apply, required commitments, fields of study expectations, participating-school logistics, and the attributes the foundation looks for in selecting fellows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant status (who may apply)
rubrics_metrics.description: All eligible applicants must be college seniors, first‑year graduate students, or in a gap period preparing to apply to graduate school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit eligibility gate—applicants outside these career stages are not eligible. Contact fellowshipinfo@hertzfoundation.org with questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended degree and enrollment model
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must intend to pursue a full‑time, in‑person PhD in the applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics or engineering at an institution in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship support is for full‑time, in‑person PhD study only; remote or part‑time PhD plans would not meet this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research direction / societal impact requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must intend to direct their studies toward understanding and solving major, near‑term problems facing society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation expects applicants to articulate how their PhD work will address real‑world, near‑term challenges (e.g., inventing new technology, developing a business, or applying interests in innovative ways). Applicants should advocate for and demonstrate how their specific field and plans will have real‑world impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a firm eligibility condition for applicants; non‑citizens/non‑permanent residents are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on professional degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation does not award fellowships to applicants pursuing professional degrees other than a PhD (such as an MD, JD, MBA, DPH, or DVM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: the foundation will support the PhD portion of an MD/PhD program. Applicants primarily pursuing terminal professional degrees (MD alone, JD, MBA, etc.) are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑discrimination policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation does not discriminate against any individual on the basis of sex, race, creed, religion, color, gender, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, registered domestic partner status, age, sexual orientation, military and veteran status, or any other basis protected by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes an inclusivity and fairness policy for application review and outreach; applicants from all protected classes are welcome to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fields of study eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Hertz Fellowships are awarded to graduate students pursuing a PhD in the applied physical and biological sciences, mathematics or engineering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation does not award fellowships based solely on a particular field; instead applicants must show how their field will be applied to address major, near‑term problems. Visit the Fellows Directory to see examples of fellows' interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation to advocate for field and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are responsible for advocating for their specific field of study and demonstrating how it will be applied to address real‑world challenges with the greatest impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the foundation does not privilege particular fields, strong applications explain the practical significance and potential societal impact of the applicant’s planned PhD work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep, integrated knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators look for applicants with deep scientific and technical knowledge who can drive exploration of complex, multidisciplinary topics and clearly articulate their ideas during in‑person conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grades and test scores are not the sole indicators—reviewers value demonstrated depth of knowledge, multidisciplinary understanding, and the ability to communicate ideas effectively in interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative problem solving
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation seeks creative problem solvers who can bring together expertise, resources, and critical thinking from different fields to create solutions greater than the sum of their parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of cross‑disciplinary thought, novel approaches, or inventive application of knowledge strengthens an applicant’s case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to the greater good
rubrics_metrics.description: Hertz Fellows direct their talents toward solving real‑world problems that impact the nation and the world; applicants should demonstrate such commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should show motivation to use scientific/technical skills for societal benefit rather than purely academic or personal interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluators look for self‑starters who can gain colleagues' trust, build consensus around ambitious visions, and deliver on promises down to details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership evidence can include research leadership, project management, team initiatives, or other activities showing initiative and follow‑through.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifelong achievement trajectory
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation favors rising stars with a track record of success at multiple stages (e.g., innovative undergraduate research, excellence in ROTC, advancing a cause) and a desire to continue growing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent achievement over time—academic, extracurricular, service, or leadership—signals potential for future impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral commitment (non‑binding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before awarding a fellowship, applicants must make a non‑binding moral commitment to make their skills available to the United States in times of national emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is explicitly non‑contractual; the foundation provides no definition of 'national emergency' and leaves interpretation to each fellow. It is a moral expectation rather than a legal obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participating‑school agreement and portability
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation has standard agreements with over 50 U.S. universities to coordinate stipend, tuition, and other costs under a 9‑month stipend model; if a fellow’s school is not listed, the foundation may negotiate with that school, and fellows may change to another participating school during the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should check the participating schools list; lack of listing is not an absolute bar—requests can be made to add a school. This governs administrative coordination of fellowship payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalist funding partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation partners with Case Western Reserve University and Texas A&M University to offer full financial benefits of a Hertz Fellowship to applicants who advance as Hertz Finalists but are not ultimately selected as Hertz Fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who reach finalist status may have alternative paths to full fellowship benefits via these partner institutions; check linked pages for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and value
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hertz Fellowship awards up to five years of funding, valued at up to $250,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the typical financial support envelope and duration applicants can expect if selected.
